title: HoP 279 - Quadrivial Pursuits - the Oxford Calculators
summary: Bradwardine and other thinkers based at Oxford make breakthroughs in physics by applying mathematics to motion.

title: HoP 278 - Sara Uckelman on Obligations
summary: Sara Uckelman soundly defeats Peter in the medieval logical game of "obligations."

title: HoP 277 - Trivial Pursuits - Fourteenth Century Logic
summary: The scholastics discuss the ambiguity of terms, the nature of logical inference, and logical paradoxes, and play the game of “obligations.”

title: HoP 276 - Back to the Future - Foreknowledge and Predestination
summary: Scotus, Ockham, and Bradwardine ask how we can be free if God knows and chooses the things we will do in the future.

title: HoP 275 - Keeping it Real - Responses to Ockham
summary: Walter Burley flies the flag for realism against Ockham and other nominalists.

title: HoP 274 - Susan Brower-Toland on Ockham's Philosophy of Mind
summary: An interview with Susan Brower-Toland covering Ockham's views on cognition, consciousness, and memory.

title: HoP 273 - What Do You Think? - Ockham on Mental Language
summary: How the language of thought relates to spoken and written language, according to William of Ockham.

title: HoP 272 - A Close Shave - Ockham’s Nominalism
summary: Ockham trims away the unnecessary entities posited by other scholastics.

title: HoP 271 - Do As You’re Told - Ockham on Ethics and Political Philosophy
summary: William of Ockham on freedom of action and freedom of thought.

title: HoP 270 - Render unto Caesar - Marsilius of Padua
summary: In his book Defender of the Peace, Marsilius of Padua develops new theories of representative government, rights, and ownership.

title: Democracy and the History of Philosophy
summary: Peter muses on recent political events in light of the history of philosophy.

title: HoP 269 - Our Power is Real - The Clash of Church and State
summary: Giles of Rome and Dante on the rival claims of the church and secular rulers.

title: HoP 268 - To Hell and Back - Dante Alighieri
summary: Italy’s greatest poet Dante Alighieri was also a philosopher, as we learn from his Convivio and of course the Divine Comedy.

title: HoP 267 - After Virtue - Marguerite Porete
summary: Marguerite Porete is put to death for her exploration of the love of God, The Mirror of Simple Souls.

title: HoP 266 - Tom Pink on the Will
summary: A conversation with Tom Pink about medieval theories of freedom and action.

title: HoP 265 - Time of the Signs - the Fourteenth Century
summary: An introduction to philosophy in the 14th century, focusing on two big ideas: nominalism and voluntarism.

title: HoP 264 - Giorgio Pini on Scotus on Knowledge
summary: Peter hears about Duns Scotus' epistemology from expert Giorgio Pini.

title: HoP 263 - One in a Million - Scotus on Universals and Individuals
summary: Scotus explains how things can share a nature in common while being unique individuals.

title: HoP 262 - On Command - Scotus on Ethics
summary: Scotus argues that morality is a matter of freely choosing to follow God’s freely issued commands.

title: HoP 261 - To Will or Not to Will - Scotus on Freedom
summary: Scotus develops a novel theory of free will and, along the way, rethinks the notions of necessity and possibility.

title: HoP 260 - Once and for All - Scotus on Being
summary: Duns Scotus attacks the proposal of Aquinas and Henry of Ghent that being is subject to analogy.

title: HoP 259 - Richard Cross on Philosophy and the Trinity
summary: Medieval discussions of the Trinity charted new metaphysical territory, as we see in this interview with Richard Cross.

title: HoP 258 - Here Comes the Son - The Trinity and the Eucharist
summary: Philosophy is pushed to its limits to provide rational explanations of two Christian theological doctrines.

title: HoP 257 - Martin Pickave on Henry of Ghent and Freedom
summary: An interview with Martin Pickavé on voluntarism in Henry of Ghent.

title: HoP 256 - Frequently Asked Questions - Henry of Ghent
summary: Henry of Ghent, now little known but a leading scholastic in the late 13th century, makes influential proposals on all the debates of his time.

title: HoP 255 - Andreas Speer on Medieval Aesthetics
summary: Does medieval art tell us anything about medieval theories of aesthetics? Peter finds out from Andreas Speer.

title: HoP 254 - Love, Reign Over Me - The Romance of the Rose
summary: Sex, reason, and religion in Jean de Meun’s completion of an allegory of courtly love, the Roman de la Rose.

title: HoP 253 - Let Me Count the Ways - Speculative Grammar
summary: The “modistae” explore the links between language, the mind, and reality.

title: HoP 252 - Neverending Story - the Eternity of the World
summary: Aquinas, Bonaventure, and the so-called “Latin Averroists” take up the question of whether the universe has always existed, and settle once and for all which comes first, the chicken or the egg.

title: HoP 251 - Masters of the University - “Latin Averroism"
summary: Did Siger of Brabant and Boethius of Dacia, who have been called “Latin Averroists” and “radical Aristotelians,” really embrace a doctrine of “double truth”?

title: HoP 250 - Q&A
summary: Peter answers listener questions on the nature of philosophy and the podcast series.

title: HoP 249 - Paris When it Sizzles - the Condemnations
summary: Two rounds of condemnations at Paris declare certain philosophical teachings as heretical. But what were the long term effects?

title: HoP 248 - Scott MacDonald on Aquinas
summary: Scott MacDonald joins Peter to discuss Thomas Aquinas' views on human knowledge.

title: HoP 247 - Onward, Christian Soldiers - Just War Theory
summary: Aquinas follows medieval legal thinkers in defining the conditions under which war may be justified, and proposes his famous doctrine of double effect.

title: HoP 246 - What Pleases the Prince - The Rule of Law
summary: Natural law and political legitimacy in thirteenth century thinkers up to and including Thomas Aquinas.

title: HoP 245 - What Comes Naturally - Ethics in Albert and Aquinas
summary: Natural and supernatural virtue and happiness in Thomas Aquinas and his teacher, Albert the Great.

title: HoP 244 - Everybody Needs Some Body - Aquinas on Soul and Knowledge
summary: Thomas Aquinas makes controversial claims concerning the unity of the soul and the empirical basis of human knowledge.

title: HoP 243 - The Ox Heard Round the World - Thomas Aquinas
summary: An introduction to Thomas Aquinas, his views on faith and reason, and his famous “five ways” of proving God’s existence.

title: HoP 242 - Therese Cory on Self-Awareness in Albert and Aquinas
summary: Therese Cory tells Peter what Albert the Great and Thomas Aquinas thought about self-awareness.

title: HoP 241 - The Shadow Knows - Albert the Great’s Metaphysics
summary: Albert the Great’s theory of being and his attempt to explain what changes in the human mind when we come to see God in the afterlife.

title: HoP 240 - Animal, Vegetable, Mineral - Albert the Great’s Natural Philosophy
summary: Albert the Great earns his nickname “universal doctor” by devoting himself to the whole of nature, from geology and botany to the study of human nature.

title: HoP 239 - Catarina Dutilh Novaes on Medieval Logic
summary: Was medieval logic "formal"? Peter finds out from Catarina Dutilh Novaes.

title: HoP 238 - Binding Arbitration - Robert Kilwardby
summary: Robert Kilwardby is infamous for his ban on teaching certain philosophical ideas at Oxford, yet made contributions in logic and on the soul.

title: HoP 237 - Begin the Beguine - Hadewijch and Mechthild of Magdeburg
summary: Two Beguine authors, Hadewijch and Mechthild of Magdeburg, deploy the tropes of courtly love in vernacular writings about their mystical experiences.

title: Indian Philosophy Announcement!
summary: New feed for Philosophy in India: http://hopwag2.podbean.com/feed/

title: HoP 236 - None for Me, Thanks - Franciscan Poverty
summary: Bonaventure and Peter Olivi respond to critics of the Franciscan vow of poverty, in a debate which produced new ideas about economics and rights.

title: HoP 235 - Juhana Toivanen on Animals in Medieval Philosophy
summary: Medieval ideas about what animals do and do not have in common with humans, and how we should treat them.

title: HoP 234 - Your Attention Please - Peter Olivi
summary: Peter Olivi proposes that awareness occurs not through passively being affected by things, but by actively paying attention to them.

title: HoP 233 - Stairway to Heaven - Bonaventure
summary: Bonaventure argues that human knowledge depends on an illumination from God.

title: HoP 232 - Charles Burnett on Magic
summary: Charles Burnett tells Peter about the role of magic in medieval intellectual life.

title: HoP 231 - Origin of Species - Roger Bacon
summary: Roger Bacon extols the power of science based on experience and uses a general theory of "species" to explain light and vision.

title: HoP 230 - A Light That Never Goes Out - Robert Grosseteste
summary: Translator, scientist and theologian Robert Grosseteste sheds light on the cosmos, human understanding, and the rainbow.

title: HoP 229 - Do the Right Thing - Thirteenth Century Ethics
summary: The scholastics explore Aristotle’s ethical teaching and the concept of moral conscience.

title: HoP 228 - It's All Good - The Transcendentals
summary: Philip the Chancellor introduces the transcendentals, a key idea in medieval metaphysics and aesthetics.

title: HoP 227 - Stayin’ Alive - Thirteenth Century Psychology
summary: John Blund and William of Auvergne draw on Aristotle and Avicenna to argue that the soul is immaterial and immortal.

title: HoP 226 - Full of Potential - Thirteenth Century Physics
summary: Richard Rufus and anonymous commentators on Aristotle explore the nature of motion, time, infinity and space.

title: HoP 225 - No Uncertain Terms - Thirteenth Century Logic
summary: The terminist logicians William of Sherwood and Peter of Spain classify the various ways that language can relate to the world.

title: HoP 224 - Kent Emery on Institutions of Learning
summary: Kent Emery joins Peter to discuss the effects of monastic and university culture on medieval philosophy.

title: HoP 223 - Straw Men - The Rise of the Universities
summary: The emergence of universities in Paris, Oxford, Bologna and elsewhere provide the main setting for medieval philosophy in the 13th century and beyond.

title: HoP 222 - Rediscovery Channel - Translations into Latin
summary: Greek and Arabic sources are rendered into Latin in a translation movement that will revolutionize medieval philosophy.

title: HoP 221 - Leading Light - Hildegard of Bingen
summary: The life, visions, political intrigues and scientific interests of Hildegard of Bingen.

title: HoP 220 - Caroline Humfress on the Roots of Medieval Law
summary: A discussion about Roman law and its reception in the medieval period, with ancient law expert Caroline Humfress.

title: HoP 219 - Law and Order - Gratian and Peter Lombard
summary: Gratian and Peter Lombard help bring scholasticism to maturity by systematizing law and theology.

title: HoP 218 - Two Swords - Early Medieval Political Philosophy
summary: The “Investiture Contest” between church and state and the first major work of medieval political philosophy, John of Salisbury’s Policraticus.

title: HoP 217 - Andrew Arlig on Parts and Wholes
summary: Andrew Arlig joins Peter to discuss medieval discussions of mereology (the study of parts and wholes).

title: HoP 216 - One of a Kind - Gilbert of Poitiers on Individuation
summary: Gilbert of Poitiers proposes a unique way to explain how each individual is the individual it is.

title: HoP 215 - The Medieval Podcasters
summary: In this special episode, Peter chats with the hosts of the History of the Crusades, History of Byzantium, and British History podcasts.

title: HoP 214 - The Good Book - Philosophy of Nature
summary: As early medieval science blossoms, Bernard Silvestris and Alan of Lille personify Nature in their philosophical prose-poems.

title: HoP 213 - On the Shoulders of Giants - Philosophy at Chartres
summary: The controversial role of Chartres in the philosophical Renaissance of the twelfth century.

title: HoP 212 - Like Father, Like Son - Debating the Trinity
summary: Discussion, debate and denunciation of philosophical attempts to explain the Trinity in Abelard, Richard of St Victor and Bernard of Clairvaux.

title: HoP 211 - Learn Everything - the Victorines
summary: Hugh of Saint Victor and other scholars of the same abbey combine secular learning with spirituality.

title: HoP 210 - John Marenbon on Peter Abelard
summary: John Marenbon returns to the podcast to discuss Abelard's views on necessity and freedom..

title: HoP 209 - It’s the Thought that Counts - Abelard’s Ethics
summary: Peter Abelard sets out an innovative ethical theory that identifies intentions as the core of moral life.

title: HoP 208 - Get Thee to a Nunnery - Heloise and Abelard
summary: Peter Abelard and Heloise prove themselves to be fascinating thinkers as well as star-crossed lovers.

title: HoP 207 - All or Nothing - The Problem of Universals
summary: Abelard and other logicians of the 12th century argue over the status of universals: are they words or things?

title: HoP 206 - Eileen Sweeney on Anselm
summary: Anselm expert Eileen Sweeney discusses his approach to philosophy and the devotional aspect of his works.

title: HoP 205 - Somebody's Perfect - Anselm's Ontological Argument
summary: The most famous argument in medieval philosophy is Anselm's proof of God's existence. But how is it supposed to work?

title: HoP 204 - A Canterbury Tale - Anselm's Life and Works
summary: Anselm offers more than his famous ontological argument, including a subtle account of human freedom.

title: HoP 203 - Virgin Territory - Peter Damian on Changing the Past
summary: Peter Damian takes up a question with surprising philosophical implications: can God restore virginity to a woman who has lost it?

title: HoP 202 - Philosophers Anonymous - the Roots of Scholasticism
summary: Little-known authors prepare the way for scholasticism with glosses on logic, metaphysical debate, and a poem about a cat.

title: HoP 201 - Stephen Gersh on Medieval Platonism
summary: Stephen Gersh (who was Peter's doctoral advisor!) joins him to discuss the sources and influence of Platonism in the Middle Ages.

title: HoP 200 - Jill Kraye and John Marenbon on Medieval Philosophy
summary: We celebrate reaching episode 200 with a special double interview on the problem of defining medieval philosophy.

title: HoP 199 - Much Ado About Nothing - Eriugena's Periphyseon
summary: Eriugena delves into the Greek tradition to produce his masterpiece of metaphysics and theology, the Periphyseon.

title: HoP 198 - Grace Notes - Eriugena and the Predestination Controversy
summary: John Scotus Eriugena debates free will with his rival Gottschalk, arguing that God predestines the saved but not the damned.

title: HoP 197 - Charles in Charge - The Carolingian Renaissance
summary: Alcuin leads a resurgence of interest in philosophy and the liberal arts at the court of Charlemagne.

title: HoP 196 - Arts of Darkness - Introduction to Medieval Philosophy
summary: Peter launches the series of podcasts on philosophy in medieval Latin Christendom with a look ahead at what’s to come.

title: HoP 195 - Anke von Kügelgen on Contemporary Islamic Thought
summary: Anke von Kügelgen joins Peter to discuss developments over the last century or so, including attitudes towards past thinkers like Avicenna, Averroes and Ibn Taymiyya.

title: HoP 194 - Iran So Far - After Ṣadrā
summary: From Sabzawārī in the 19th century to Seyyed Hossein Nasr today, Iranian thinkers promote and respond to the thought of Mullā Ṣadrā.

title: HoP 193 - All for One and One for All - Muḥammad 'Abdūh and Muḥammad Iqbāl
summary: Muḥammad 'Abdūh and Muḥammad Iqbāl challenge colonialism and the traditional religious scholars of Islam.

title: HoP 192 - The Stronger Sex - Women Scholars and Islam
summary: Fatema Mernissi and others challenge the long-standing (but not complete) exclusion of women from the intellectual traditions of Islam.

title: HoP 191 - The Young Ones: Encounters with European Thought
summary: 18th and 19th century intellectuals in India and the Ottoman empire, from Shāh Walī Allāh to the Young Turks, continue Islamic traditions and grapple with European science.

title: HoP 190 - Turkish Delights - Philosophy under the Ottomans
summary: Kātib Çelebi defends cigarettes and coffee, in just one of several philosophical and religious debates in the Ottoman empire.

title: HoP 189 - Subcontinental Drift - Philosophy in Islamic India
summary: Ideas spread to Mughal India from Iran, and prince Dārā Shikūh seeks to unite the wisdom of the Upanishads with the Koran.

title: HoP 188 - Sajjad Rizvi on Mulla Sadra
summary: Sajjad Rizvi talks to Peter about Mullā Ṣadrā's views on eternity, God's knowledge and the afterlife.

title: HoP 187 - Return to Sender - Mulla Sadra on Motion and Knowledge
summary: Mullā Ṣadrā proposes that all things are like sharks: in constant motion.

title: HoP 186 - To Be, Continued - Mulla Sadra on Existence
summary: Mullā Ṣadrā, greatest thinker of early modern Iran, unveils his radical new understanding of existence.

title: HoP 185 - Follow the Leader - Philosophy under the Safavids
summary: Philosophy in Safavid Iran, and a look back at earlier philosophy among Shiites.

title: HoP 184 - Robert Wisnovsky on Commentary Culture
summary: Robert Wisnovsky joins Peter to discuss the enormous body of unstudied philosophical commentaries in the later Eastern Islamic world.

title: HoP 183 - Family Feud - Philosophy at Shiraz
summary: The roots of the Safavid philosophical tradition in some rather ill-tempered debates at Shīrāz.

title: HoP 182 - Aftermath - Philosophy and Science in the Mongol Age
summary: Philosophy and science survive and even thrive through the coming of the Mongols.

title: HoP 181 - By the Book - Ibn Taymiyya
summary: The controversial jurist Ibn Taymiyya sets forth an originalist theory of law and a searching criticism of the philosophers’ logic.

title: HoP 180 - Proof Positive - The Logical Tradition
summary: Later Islamic logicians try to solve the Liar Paradox and take on the advances of Avicenna's logic.

title: HoP 179 - Mohammed Rustom on Philosophical Sufism
summary: Peter is joined by Mohammed Rustom in a discussion about Sufi authors including Ibn 'Arabī and Rūmī

title: HoP 178 - Eyes Wide Shut - Rumi and Philosophical Sufism
summary: The Persian poet Rūmī and mystical philosopher al-Qūnawī carry on the legacy of Sufism.

title: HoP 177 - To Be or Not to Be - Debating Avicenna’s Metaphysics
summary: Avicenna’s distinction between essence and existence triggers a running debate among philosophers and theologians.

title: HoP 176 - A Man for all Seasons - al-Tusi
summary: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī’s controversial career sees him adopt and then abandon Ismāʿīlism, team up with the Mongols, and offer a staunch defense of Avicenna.

title: HoP 175 - Bright Ideas - Illuminationism
summary: The Illuminationists carry on Suhrawardī’s critique of “Peripatetic” philosophy and wonder if they will be reborn as giraffes.

title: HoP 174 - Leading Light - Suhrawardi
summary: Suhrawardī, founder of the Illuminationist (ishrāqī) tradition, proposes a metaphysics of light on the basis of his theory of knowledge by presence

title: HoP 173 - For the Sake of Argument - Fakhr al-Din al-Razi
summary: The hugely influential Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī weaves Avicenna and Islamic theology into complex dialectical treatments of time, God, the soul, and ethics.

title: HoP 172 - All Things Considered - Abu l-Barakat al-Baghdadi
summary: Abū l-Barakāt al-Baghdādī makes up his own mind about physics and the soul, and along the way inaugurates a new style of doing philosophy.

title: HoP 171 - Golden Ages - The Later Eastern Traditions
summary: An introduction to later developments in philosophical theology, sufism, and Illuminationism, focusing on the reception and critique of Avicenna.

title: HoP 170 - Gad Freudenthal on Jewish Philosophy and Science
summary: Leading scholar of medieval Jewish thought Gad Freudenthal joins Peter in a concluding episode on Andalusian thought.

title: HoP 169 - A Matter of Principles - Albo and Abravanel
summary: Joseph Albo and Isaac Abravanel critique Maimonides’ attempt to lay down foundations for the Jewish law.

title: HoP 168 - Chariot of Fire - Kabbalah
summary: The rich symbolism of the Zohar and the spiritual practices of Abraham Abluafia feature in the mystical movement known as Kabbalah.

title: HoP 167 - When Bad Things Happen to Good People - Suffering in Jewish Philosophy
summary: The Book of Job provokes Saadia, Maimonides, Ibn Tibbon and Gersonides to reflect on why God allows suffering.

title: HoP 166 - Tamar Rudavsky on Gersonides and Crescas
summary: Tamar Rudavsky joins Peter to talk about the two great medieval Jewish thinkers after Maimonides: Gersonides and Crescas.

title: HoP 165 - Neither the Time Nor the Place - Hasdai Crescas
summary: Ḥasdai Crescas shows Aristotelian physics who’s boss, by defending alternative conceptions of time, place and infinity.

title: HoP 164 - Man and Superman - Gersonides and the Jewish Reaction to Averroes
summary: The super-commentator Gersonides and other Jews digest the ideas of Averroes.

title: HoP 163 - Burnt Offerings - The Maimonides Controversy
summary: Maimonides’ works provoke a bitter dispute among Jews in France and Spain over the relation of philosophy to Judaism.

title: HoP 162 - Sarah Stroumsa on Maimonides
summary: Maimonides as a "Mediterranean thinker": Peter is joined by Sarah Stroumsa.

title: HoP 161 - He Moves in Mysterious Ways - Maimonides on Eternity
summary: Maimonides tries to settle the eternity of the world debate by declaring a draw.

title: HoP 160 - The Great Eagle - Maimonides
summary: The great Jewish philosopher and legal scholar Maimonides, and the ideas in his Mishneh Torah and Guide for the Perplexed.

title: HoP 159 - With All Your Heart - Ethics and Judaism
summary: Baḥya Ibn Paquda and Maimonides explore the ethical dimension of the Jewish scriptures and legal tradition.

title: HoP 158 - Born Under a Bad Sign - Freedom and Astrology in Jewish Philosophy
summary: Abraham Ibn Ezra, Ibn Daud and Maimonides consider the philosophical implications of astrology as science flourishes in the Jewish culture of Andalusia.

title: HoP 157 - Choosing My Religion - Judah Hallevi
summary: Judah Hallevi argues that Judaism has a better claim to belief than philosophy, Christianity, or Islam.

title: HoP 156 - Sarah Pessin on Jewish Neoplatonism
summary: Peter chats with Sarah Pessin about the Neoplatonism of Jewish philosophers such as Isaac Israeli, Ibn Gabirol, and Maimonides.

title: HoP 155 - Matter over Mind - Ibn Gabirol
summary: Neoplatonism returns in Ibn Gabriol, who controversially holds that everything apart from God has both matter and form.

title: HoP 154 - The Philosophy of History - Ibn Khaldun
summary: The historian Ibn Khaldūn applies the methods of philosophy to understand the rise and fall of political regimes.

title: HoP 153 - A Matter of Taste – Ibn Arabi and Mysticism
summary: Sufism, the mystical tradition of Islam, collides with philosophy in the work of Ibn ʿArabī.

title: HoP 152 - Richard Taylor on Averroes
summary: Averroes scholar Richard C. Taylor joins Peter to talk about Averroes' views on the relation between Islam and philosophy.

title: HoP 151 - Single Minded - Averroes on the Intellect
summary: Averroes defends the rather surprising notion that all of mankind shares a single intellect.

title: HoP 150 - Charles Burnett and Dag N Hasse on Arabic Latin Translations
summary: A special 150th double interview episode on the transmission of philosophy from Arabic into Latin.

title: HoP 149 - Back to Basics - Averroes on Reason and Religion
summary: An introduction to “the Commentator” Averroes, and his defense of philosophy in the Decisive Treatise.

title: HoP 148 - Fantasy Island - Ibn Bajja and Ibn Tufayl
summary: Intellect and alienation in Ibn Bājja and Ibn Ṭufayl, author of the philosophical desert island castaway tale “Ḥayy Ibn Yaqẓān.”

title: HoP 147 - Laying Down the Law – Ibn Hazm and Islamic Legal Theory
summary: The development of Islamic law and jurisprudence (fiqh), and the many-sided output of the legal theorist Ibn Ḥazm.

title: HoP 146 - Philosophy's Reign in Spain - Andalusia
summary: The flowering of philosophy among Muslims and Jews in al-Andalus (Muslim-controlled Spain and Portugal).

title: HoP 145 - Frank Griffel on al-Ghazali
summary: Why did al-Ghazālī judge "the philosophers" to be apostates? Peter finds out from Frank Griffel.

title: HoP 144 - Miracle Worker - al-Ghazali against the Philosophers
summary: In his “Incoherence of the Philosophers,” al-Ghazālī attacks Avicenna’s theories about the eternity of the universe and insists on the possibility of miracles.

title: HoP 143 - Special Delivery - al-Ghazali
summary: Al-Ghazālī’s search for truth leads him to philosophy, Asharite theology, and ultimately the mystical tradition of Sufism.

title: HoP 142 - Dimitri Gutas on Avicenna
summary: Peter talks to Dimitri Gutas about Avicenna's sources, philosophical methods, and influence.

title: HoP 141 - Into Thin Air - Avicenna on the Soul
summary: With his Flying Man argument, Avicenna explores self-awareness and the relation between soul and body.

title: HoP 140 - By All Means Necessary - Avicenna on God
summary: Avicenna’s proof of the Necessary Existent is ingenious and influential; but does it amount to a proof of God’s existence?

title: HoP 139 - By the Time I Get to Phoenix - Avicenna on Existence
summary: Avicenna revolutionizes metaphysics with groundbreaking ideas about necessity and contingency, and his new distinction between essence and existence.

title: HoP 138 - The Self-Made Man - Avicenna's Life and Works
summary: Despite a tumultuous life, Avicenna manages to become the most influential of all medieval philosophers.

title: HoP 137 - God Willing – the Asharites
summary: Al-Ash‘arī puts his stamp on the future of Islamic theology by emphasizing God’s untrammeled power and freedom.

title: HoP 136 - Farhad Daftary on the Ismailis
summary: Peter is joined by Farhad Daftary, a leading expert on the Shiite group known as the Ismā'īlīs.

title: HoP 135 - Undercover Brothers – Philosophy in the Buyid Age
summary: Miskawayh, al-‘Amiri, al-Tawhidi, the Brethren of Purity and Ismaili missionaries bring together philosophy with Persian culture, literature and Islam.

title: HoP 134 - Balancing Acts - Arabic Ethical Literature
summary: Drawing on Galen and Aristotle, philosophers from al-Kindi to Miskawayh compose ethical works designed us to achieve health in soul, as well as body.

title: HoP 133 - Strings Attached - Music and Philosophy
summary: Peter turns DJ, with some actual music interspersed with discussion about theories of music in Arabic philosophical texts.

title: HoP 132 - Eye of the Beholder - Theories of Vision
summary: Ibn al-Haytham draws on the tradition of geometrical optics to explain the mystery of human eyesight.

title: HoP 131 - Deborah Black on al-Farabi's Epistemology
summary: Deborah Black joins Peter to talk about al-Farabi's innovations concerning knowledge and certainty.

title: HoP 130 - State of Mind - al-Farabi on Religion and Politics
summary: Al-Fārābī combines Islam and Greek sources to present the ideal ruler as a philosopher who is also a prophet.

title: HoP 129 - The Second Master - al-Farabi
summary: Peter begins to look at the systematic rethinking of Hellenic philosophy offered by al-Farabi, focusing on his logic and metaphysics.

title: HoP 128 - Aristotelian Society - the Baghdad School
summary: A group of mostly Christian philosophers transpose the practices of antique Aristotelian philosophy to 10th century Baghdad.

title: HoP 127 - Peter E Pormann on Medicine in the Islamic World
summary: A double dose of Peters, as Pormann joins Adamson to discuss medicine and philosophy in the Islamic world.

title: HoP 126 - High Five - al-Razi
summary: The doctor and philosopher Abu Bakr al-Razi sets out a daring philosophical theory involving five eternal principles: God, soul, matter, time and place.

title: HoP 125 - Reasoned Belief - Saadia Gaon
summary: Saadia Gaon draws on Greek philosophy and Islamic theology to provide a rational account of Jewish belief.

title: HoP 124 - The Chosen Ones - Judaism and Philosophy
summary: The roots of Jewish philosophy in the Islamic world, focusing on the Rabbinic background in the Mishnah and Talmud, and the thought of early figures like Isaac Israeli.

title: HoP 123 - Philosopher of the Arabs - al-Kindi
summary: Al-Kindī uses Hellenic materials to discuss the eternity of the world, divine attributes, and the nature of the soul.

title: HoP 122 - Founded in Translation - From Greek to Syriac and Arabic
summary: Greek philosophy and science make their way into the Islamic world via Syriac and Arabic translations and interpretations.

title: HoP 121 - This is a Test - the Mutazilites
summary: A first look at the philosophical contributions of Islamic theology (kalām) and its political context, focusing on the Muʿtazilites Abū l-Hudhayl and al-Naẓẓām.

title: HoP 120 - The Straight Path - Philosophy in the Islamic World
summary: The rise of Islam creates a new context for philosophy not only among Muslims, but also Jews and Christians. .

title: HoP 119 - John Marenbon on Boethius
summary: John Marenbon joins Peter to discuss Boethius' solution to the problem of divine foreknowledge.

title: HoP 118 - Fate, Hope and Clarity - Boethius
summary: Boethius ushers in the medieval age with expert works on Aristotle, subtle treatises on theology, and the Consolation of Philosophy, written while he awaited execution.

title: HoP 117 - Born Again - Latin Platonism
summary: Apuleius, Victorinus, Martianus Cappella, Macrobius and Calcidius present and interpret Platonic teachings for readers of Latin.

title: HoP 116 - Charles Brittain on Augustine's On the Trinity
summary: In a final episode on Augustine, Charles Brittain joins Peter to discuss On the Trinity.

title: HoP 115 - Me, Myself and I - Augustine on Mind and Memory
summary: In On the Trinity Augustine explores the human mind as an image of God.

title: HoP 114 - Sarah Byers on Augustine's Ethics
summary: Peter speaks with Sarah Byers about the Stoic influence on Augustine's ethics and theory of action.

title: HoP 113 - Heaven and Earth - Augustine’s City of God
summary: In his City of God Augustine traces the histories and philosophical underpinnings of two “cities,” one devoted to worldly glory, the other to heavenly bliss.

title: HoP 112 - Help Wanted - Augustine on Freedom
